editorNote: The first week of November brings the office micro and the living-room console into the same holiday newspaper frame: IBM compatibility, cartridge shelves, vector graphics, and pop charts all crowd the counter.
morningLine: This week the luggable PC clone becomes the serious office rumor, while game departments prepare Atari 5200 and Vectrex demonstrations for Christmas shoppers.

lead.headline: Compaq Shows a Portable Route Into the IBM PC World
lead.summary: Compaq used November 1982 to unveil a 28-pound portable computer built for strong IBM PC compatibility, a $2,995 luggable that pointed toward the coming clone market while business buyers still measured software shelves by WordStar, spreadsheets, and databases.
lead.confidence: November 1982 announcement; price and compatibility details from retrospective hardware reporting

computerItems.label: Console Counter
computerItems.headline: Atari 5200 Reaches Holiday Shelves
computerItems.summary: Atari’s higher-end 5200 was appearing in limited store distribution around October and November, bundled with Super Breakout and aimed at ColecoVision and Intellivision shoppers.

computerItems.label: Vector Display
computerItems.headline: Vectrex Adds a Tiny Arcade Monitor to the Living Room
computerItems.summary: The Vectrex arrives as one of 1982’s strangest home systems, using its own monochrome vector screen and overlay sheets instead of the family television.

computerItems.label: Home Computer Desk
computerItems.headline: Sub-$100 and 64K Machines Pull New Buyers In
computerItems.summary: The Timex Sinclair 1000 and Commodore 64 keep widening the home-computing ladder, from bargain BASIC experimentation to a more ambitious color-and-sound machine.

computerItems.label: Magazine Rack
computerItems.headline: November Computer Magazines Crowd the Desk
computerItems.summary: Personal Computer World’s November issue points to DEC Rainbow, Apple II, HP-75, calculators, and portable-computing talk as readers compare practical machines.

market.headline: The Holiday Counter Splits Between IBM Compatibility and Cartridge Play
market.summary: Business buyers ask whether a portable can run PC software; families ask which machine has the arcade names. The same store may be explaining WordStar in one aisle and Donkey Kong in the next.

curiosity.headline: First Blood Leads the November Movie Counter
curiosity.summary: Domestic November box-office totals put First Blood ahead for the month, with E.T. still showing extraordinary staying power after its summer opening.
